subtype: Hitting a sibling after being scolded [Actor]
passage:
In the kitchen of their flat in Uppsala, Pappa took away the red crayon. "No drawing on the wall, Astrid." Astrid, almost three, went stiff and didn't look at him. She turned and shoved her little sister Ingrid, who was stacking cups on the rug. Ingrid toppled over and cried.
Pappa scooped up Ingrid, then knelt by Astrid. "You're cross with me. That's okay. Pushing isn't. Stamp your feet instead?"
Astrid stamped, hard.

qa.q: What was Ingrid doing when Astrid pushed her?
qa.a: Stacking cups on the rug.

qa.q: Why did Astrid push Ingrid instead of showing Pappa she was cross?
qa.a: Astrid was angry with Pappa, but he felt too big to be cross with, so the anger landed on her little sister, who felt safer.

qa.q: What did Pappa choose to do after comforting Ingrid?
qa.a: He named Astrid's anger at him, said pushing isn't okay, and offered a safe way to let it out by stamping.

qa.q: What is it like for Ingrid when she gets pushed?
qa.a: Ingrid is just stacking cups and suddenly topples over, a shock she can't make sense of 😢

grounding: A toddler told off by her father turns and pushes her smaller sister, and the father names the anger and offers a safer outlet.

subtype: Hitting a sibling after being scolded [Actor]
passage:
I was fixing the tap at my sister's flat when her daughter Ankita, two and a half, poured her water onto the floor. "Ankita, no!" my sister said sharply.
Ankita's face crumpled. She didn't cry. She grabbed her wooden duck and flung it across the room at the cot where baby Rohit lay. It hit the bars.
I can't know what goes on in a two-year-old's head. But she didn't throw it at her mother.
My sister picked her up. "You're upset I said no." Ankita hid her face.
— Francis

qa.q: What did Ankita throw?
qa.a: Her wooden duck.

qa.q: Why might Ankita have thrown the duck at the cot rather than at her mother?
qa.a: Ankita seemed angry at being told no, but her mother felt too big to be angry at, so the feeling flew toward the baby instead.

qa.q: What choice did Ankita's mother make that helped?
qa.a: She picked Ankita up and named the feeling, "You're upset I said no", so Ankita felt understood instead of scolded again.

qa.q: How might Francis have felt watching the duck hit the cot?
qa.a: Francis was probably startled and worried for baby Rohit, and struck that Ankita aimed at the cot, not at her mother.

grounding: An uncle or aunt sees a two-year-old scolded by her mother throw a toy at the baby's cot instead.

subtype: Hitting a sibling after being scolded [Actor]
passage:
Monday. Amma said, "No, Sangeeta, not the remote." Sangeeta, three, dropped it, then marched over to her baby brother Babu and pulled his hair. Babu howled.
Wednesday. Told off for tipping out the rice, she threw her doll at Babu's feet. Lakshmi, her Amma, knelt down. "You're cross with Amma. Throw this pillow at the bed instead." Sangeeta threw it hard.
Next week. After another "no", she stomped to the bed and whacked the pillow. Babu kept on playing.

qa.q: Whose hair did Sangeeta pull on Monday?
qa.a: Her baby brother Babu's hair.

qa.q: Why does Sangeeta go after Babu when Amma is the one who said no?
qa.a: Sangeeta is cross with Amma, but Amma is too big and important to be angry at, so the anger lands on smaller Babu.

qa.q: Which choice of Lakshmi's gave Sangeeta's anger a safe place?
qa.a: Naming that Sangeeta was cross with Amma and offering a pillow to throw at the bed, which Sangeeta used on her own the next week.

qa.q: How might Babu experience that first week?
qa.a: Babu gets hurt out of nowhere while playing, so for him Sangeeta's anger comes with no reason he can see.

grounding: Over a week a three-year-old who takes her mother's telling-off out on her baby brother learns to hit a pillow instead.

subtype: Hitting a sibling after being scolded [Actor]
passage: In their Dadar flat, Aai lifted Omkar's muddy hands out of the plant pot. "No, Omkar. Soil stays in the pot." Omkar, two and a half, stamped his foot and scowled at her. Then he spun round and pushed his baby brother Tushar, who was crawling past. Tushar rolled onto the rug and wailed. Aai scooped up both boys. "You're cross with me," she said. "Stamp your feet. No pushing Tushar."

qa.q: Where were Omkar's muddy hands when Aai lifted them?
qa.a: Omkar's muddy hands were in the plant pot.

qa.q: Why did Omkar push Tushar instead of showing his anger to Aai?
qa.a: Omkar was cross with Aai for stopping him, but she was big and in charge; Tushar, small and crawling past, was an easier place for the anger to land.

qa.q: Which part of Aai's reply could help Omkar most next time?
qa.a: Naming that Omkar was cross with her and giving him a safe way to show it, stamping his feet, while keeping a firm no to pushing.

qa.q: What is it like for Tushar when the anger lands on him?
qa.a: Tushar did nothing wrong and is suddenly knocked over, so he is startled and hurt; he needs comfort just as much as Omkar needs a limit.

grounding: Shows a toddler, stopped by a parent, turning his anger on a smaller baby brother who feels safer to push.

subtype: Hitting a sibling after being scolded [Actor]
passage:
"Pallavi, no! Papa's phone doesn't go in the bucket."
"Mine!"
"Give it here, beta."
Pallavi, almost three, let go, lip wobbling. "Papa bad!"
She stomped to the mat where baby Gopika sat, and threw her plastic cup straight at Gopika.
"Waaah!"
"Hey, hey." Papa picked up Gopika and knelt. "Pallavi, you're angry at Papa. At Papa. Not Gopika."
"Papa bad," Pallavi said, quieter.
"You can tell Papa. You can hit the cushion. Gopika stays safe."
Pallavi thumped the cushion twice, then leaned into his knee.

qa.q: What did Pallavi throw at Gopika?
qa.a: Pallavi threw her plastic cup straight at Gopika.

qa.q: What was Pallavi feeling when she said "Papa bad!"?
qa.a: She was angry and upset that Papa took the phone 😠, but Papa was big and needed, so the anger went toward baby Gopika instead.

qa.q: What choice did Papa make after the cup hit Gopika, and why did it help?
qa.a: Papa kept Gopika safe first, then knelt and named that Pallavi was angry at him, offering the cushion as a safe outlet so the feeling had somewhere to go.

qa.q: If you were Gopika, what would you want from Papa after the cup?
qa.a: To be picked up and comforted quickly, and to feel sure that Papa would not let it happen again.

grounding: Illustrates a toddler told no by a parent who throws a toy at the baby, Gopika, the smaller and less threatening target.
